_why: The one board to open when somebody asks 'is it up'. Everything on it is a
series this repo PROVES it emits (packages/datadog/__tests__/dashboards-agreement.test.ts
asserts the whole set against the emitting source) or a vendor series named
in that test's explicit exemption list. A widget over a metric nobody emits
renders as an empty graph, which is indistinguishable from a healthy quiet
system — MONEY-1238, shipped at four layers of this stack already.

definition.title: Realtime holder healthy (1 = yes)
definition._why: A gauge, emitted on every flush tick, so SILENCE is itself the signal — this is the one process in the estate whose death is the whole feature.

definition.title: Workers: hits vs errors
definition._why: `hono.request` is the workers' SERVER span, declared once in DD_SERVER_SPAN (packages/datadog/src/constants.ts) and held to it by dashboards-agreement.test.ts. It was `web.request` until MONEY-1380 started the workers with `--import dd-trace/register.js` (~2026-09-11) and dd-trace's Hono plugin renamed the span; this widget then charted nothing (MONEY-1534). Measured 2026-09-23: 15,787 hono.request hits in 24h, no web.request series since 2026-09-11. Never `http.request`, the same library's HTTP CLIENT span — this widget read it for a release and charted our outbound calls to NSE, BSE, Screener, Tiingo and Gemini under a title claiming our own request handling.

definition.title: us-fundamentals: hits vs errors
definition._why: ddtrace-py names the FastAPI SERVER span `fastapi.request` (ddtrace/contrib/internal/fastapi/patch.py). The span is a per-service fact declared in DD_SERVER_SPAN (packages/datadog/src/constants.ts), and a convention rather than a guarantee — a DD_TRACE_SPAN_ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA change or a new integration renames it and this widget goes quiet with no error anywhere, which is what happened to the workers' widget above (MONEY-1534).
